SEC-HD-V6-01.note: Head noun is 'mat' (singular); 'bacteria...bones' are all inside modifiers. D leaves the sentence with no finite verb.

SEC-HD-V6-02.note: Nominative absolute; C's comma would split the absolute's subject from its participle, and there is no noun for it to appose.

SEC-HD-V6-03.note: Proximity rule: nearer element 'the students' is plural; D's present perfect clashes with the past frame ('the midwives had').

SEC-HD-V6-04.note: Fraction-of takes number from 'foragers'; B is number-neutral but its past tense fights the generic present frame and the 'has lost' relative.

SEC-HD-V6-05.note: 'Where the adults go...' is a clausal subject, hence singular; C and D turn the only finite verb into a relative and leave a fragment.

SEC-HD-V6-06.note: Comma closes the long 'Because...' clause; C's semicolon would follow a dependent clause.

SEC-HD-V6-07.note: 'Secreted at a cost...' must attach to 'wax'; B and D dangle, C is nonfinite.

SEC-HD-V6-08.note: SECOND ANSWER: 'recorded' licenses both NP and wh-clause objects, so 'the depth..., the character..., and how the tide sets, but' is grammatical edited English - merely non-parallel in style. A and C differ only on parallelism; both punctuate the coordinated clause correctly.

SEC-HD-V6-09.note: 'Since that paper appeared' forces present perfect; head noun is 'practice'.

SEC-HD-V6-10.note: Relative verb agrees with 'the bees'; main verb with 'The number'.

SEC-HD-V6-11.note: Dash opened must be closed with a dash; verb agrees with 'the calls' across the supplement.

SEC-HD-V6-12.note: Gerund subject 'turning...' needs a semicolon; B is a comma splice, D and A leave 'turn' without a subject.

SEC-HD-V6-13.note: 'Each of' is singular; C's past tense conflicts with the generic present ('tells').

SEC-HD-V6-14.note: Embedded question keeps statement order; 'clams' is plural.

SEC-HD-V6-15.note: Two noun phrases joined by 'and'; the post-colon 'makes/makes' fixes the present.

SEC-HD-V6-16.note: Colon before a list of noun phrases; D's 'which are' has singular 'something' as antecedent.

SEC-HD-V6-17.note: Head noun 'line' needs a finite singular verb; A and C leave a fragment.

SEC-HD-V6-18.note: 'not because X but because Y'; C strands 'was falling' without a subject, B mismatches 'prices' with 'was'.

SEC-HD-V6-19.note: RESOLVED AFTER BLANK: the very next words 'that work' (plus 'are stung', 'blame') force the plural 'beekeepers', killing C two words after the blank; only the comma-before-'so' choice then remains.

SEC-HD-V6-20.note: Third element of a to-infinitive series must keep the infinitive.

SEC-HD-V6-21.note: Participial phrase after a complete clause; C is a comma splice, D coordinates a participle with a finite verb.

SEC-HD-V6-22.note: A span of fifteen years already under way at a stated past point requires the past perfect progressive; A cannot reach back before 1984.

SEC-HD-V6-23.note: Fused relative takes nominative case from its own clause ('whoever had done'), not from 'between'.

SEC-HD-V6-24.note: Head noun is 'rise'; 'and of the shrimp' is a second prepositional phrase, not a conjoined subject.
